strategy.summary: Reproduce numba issue 10069 / PR 10088: jitted np.unique (used by np.union1d) mishandles NaN because consecutive NaNs are compared with != and never deduplicated. The developer's test adds check(np.array([np.nan, np.nan])) to test_array_methods.py, which compares the njit union1d/unique result against the py_func result via assert_equal. On the buggy revision the jitted result keeps duplicate NaNs and the shapes mismatch, so the test fails; on the fixed revision the NaN-aware dedup yields matching shapes and the test passes. Build Numba from source at the buggy commit 934a8e4426ff and at its fixed parent, since the change is in numba/np/arrayobj.py and requires compiling the extension.

system_packages: llvm (version matching llvmlite requirement, unpinned in evidence)
pinned_because: numpy version not pinned by repo: reporter used numpy 2.1.3 per issue#10069 only, which is not a documented constraint, so it is a reporter-era observation rather than a repo requirement
llvmlite/LLVM version not pinned: README names LLVM only, no version given, so the llvmlite version compatible with the checked-out numba must be chosen from its setup constraints
numba version is the project under test, not a dependency pin

strategy.reproducing_test: numba/tests/test_array_methods.py: the test method containing check(np.array([np.nan, np.nan])) (the unique test in TestArrayMethods, added by the PR diff at approximately line 1777)
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 934a8e4426ff the added check(np.array([np.nan, np.nan])) fails with an AssertionError from np.testing.assert_equal, because the jitted np.unique returns two NaNs where the py_func reference returns one (shape mismatch). On the fixed revision the same check passes because consecutive NaNs are treated as duplicates and both results are a single NaN.
strategy.numerical_probe: np.union1d(np.array([np.nan]), np.array([np.nan])) and np.union1d(np.array([np.nan, 1]), np.array([np.nan])) compared inside @njit against .py_func(); only the transition matters, not the printed values

input_output_examples.buggy_output: output differs from the Python version (printed output truncated in passage: '[na')

risks: Dtype of the failing inputs is not stated in evidence; the test uses np.array([np.nan, np.nan]) which is float64 by default, so the transition should hold for float64 but other dtypes are unverified.
The buggy output for the single-NaN case is truncated in the passage, so the exact buggy value is not confirmed; the transition is what matters.
NaN sort position relative to other values is not stated; the test should not depend on it.
The PR discussion questioned whether union1d has an independent logic error; if so, the fix may be partly unrelated to unique and the transition could be affected.

Numba JIT compilation requires llvmlite and a matching LLVM; if the build environment's LLVM differs from the era's, the buggy behaviour may not reproduce, and no platform-specific (e.g. architecture or sanitiser) requirement is documented in the evidence, so none is assumed.
Oracle is exact equality (np.testing.assert_equal) per the evidence, not a tolerance; no tolerance or ulp criterion applies.

Build from source is required because the defect sits in compiled-path Python code under numba/np/arrayobj.py at the jitted level; an installed wheel from a different version will not carry the fix or the buggy code path.
Exact fixed-parent commit hash is not given in the context; it must be determined from the PR merge base.

oracle.why: Oracle is np.testing.assert_equal between jitted result and py_func result; the expected NaN-deduplicated result is exact.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On buggy 934a8e4426ff the jitted np.unique keeps both NaNs since b[i] != x is True for NaN, so the result has shape (2,) while py_func returns shape (1,); assert_equal raises AssertionError on the shape mismatch, so the test fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the dedup condition not (np.isnan(b[i]) and np.isnan(x)) treats consecutive NaNs as duplicates, giving shape (1,) matching py_func; assert_equal passes.
